description: High-level 'head somewhere' verb. Accepts a target by identity (target_object_id, target_sim_id, object_name substring match) or by tile coordinates (location with x/y in TILE units — the handler converts to the wire's 1/16-tile units for you). Picks the closest reachable candidate and either walks to it (no interaction) or walks-and-does (when --interaction is given, the pie-menu is searched for a matching entry and interact-with is dispatched under the hood). queue_mode controls how the resolved action lands on your queue: 'queue' (default) cancels engine-autopilot Mode.Idle entries first, 'preempt' cancels everything. Use this instead of walk-to whenever you can name your destination — it removes the 1/16-tile unit conversion and the separate walk+interact chain from your workflow. Prefer target_object_id > object_name > location in that order: ids are stable, names can match multiple objects (picker takes closest), raw tile coords are the escape hatch.

args.name: my_name
args.description: A name you've previously bound with the 'name' verb. Resolves via your private name map (sidecar-side) to the right selector. Highest-precedence selector — overrides everything else if set. Discover what you've named with list-names.

args.name: target_object_id
args.description: ObjectID of a specific target. Next-highest precedence after my_name.

args.name: object_name
args.description: Case-insensitive substring match against entity names. Picker returns the closest match within max_distance_tiles. Example: object_name='Toilet' matches 'Hygeia-O-Matic Toilet'.

args.name: location
args.description: {"x": tile_x, "y": tile_y, "level": 1}. Tile-unit coordinates (handler converts to 1/16-tile internally). Use only when you need a specific tile and there is no object there.

args.name: interaction
args.description: Optional. When omitted: walk-only. When given: the target's pie-menu is searched for an entry whose name matches (exact-token first, then substring); interact-with is dispatched with the resolved TTAB id. Example: --object_name Toilet --interaction Use.

args.name: queue_mode
args.description: How the resolved action lands on your queue. 'queue' cancels engine-autopilot Idle entries; 'preempt' cancels everything.

args.name: max_distance_tiles
args.description: Reject matches further than this many tiles from the caller. Default 50 covers most lot distances. Lower it if you want a strictly-local pick.

call_signatures: cf $CF go-to --my_name "the toilet" --interaction Use             # you named it once; now just go use it
cf $CF go-to --object_name Toilet                                # walk to the nearest object whose name contains 'Toilet'
cf $CF go-to --object_name Toilet --interaction Use              # walk to the nearest Toilet and use it
cf $CF go-to --object_name Newspaper --interaction Read          # walk to the nearest newspaper and read it
cf $CF go-to --target_object_id 322 --interaction Use             # you already know the id — just go do it
cf $CF go-to --object_name Sofa --interaction Sit --queue_mode preempt   # drop what I'm doing and go sit down
cf $CF go-to --location '{"x":42,"y":59,"level":1}'            # walk to tile (42,59) — tile units, NOT 1/16-tile
common_mistakes: Passing 1/16-tile units to --location. Unlike walk-to, this verb expects TILE units (multiply by 16 happens internally). Pass --location '{"x":42,"y":59}' to reach tile (42,59).
Specifying both --object_name and --target_object_id. Precedence is target_sim_id > target_object_id > location > object_name; the lower-precedence selector is ignored. Pick one.
Expecting --interaction to match a hint/description. It matches pie-menu entry NAMES only (e.g. 'Use', 'Sit', 'Read'). Discover names with query-pie-menu first if unsure.
Trying to go-to a deleted object id (e.g. furniture that got moved or sold). Returns ok=false; re-query nearby_objects for current state.
perception_hints: What interactions a target exposes: perception.nearby_objects[].interactions[].name (use these as --interaction values)
Your queue state: perception.avatar.action_queue[]. go-to with default queue_mode clears engine-Idle entries; with --queue_mode preempt it clears your self-queued actions too.
refuse_conditions: no selector passed → ok:false with 'requires one of target_object_id, target_sim_id, object_name, location'
object_name matches no entity within max_distance_tiles → ok:false with a sample of nearby entity names
target_object_id / target_sim_id not in local VM → ok:false
--interaction has no matching pie-menu entry on the picked target → ok:false with list of available interaction names
